newsitem.title: UK: BT Eurobond spreads widen on merger plans.
newsitem.headline: BT Eurobond spreads widen on merger plans.

text.p: Eurobond spreads on British Telecommunications PLC widened by up to 20 basis points on Monday after BT said at the weekend it would merge with the second largest U.S. telecommunications company MCI, dealers said.
They said spreads could widen further if BT's credit ratings were downgraded. "They still look very tight," a trader said.
Standard & Poor's Corp said it may cut BT's AAA senior unsecured debt rating and might raise MCI Communications Corp's A-grade long-term ratings.
"BT will now be highly-geared so they are likely to be downgraded," one dealer said. "They're paying out for the merger and a special dividend which is going to cost them."
MCI, also the world's third largest international carrier, plans to merge with BT making it the largest merger in Britain's corporate history.

Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it would issue an annoucement concerning the rating implications of the merger. Moody's rates BT's senior unsecured debt AAA and MCI's senior unsecured debt A2.
The paper most affected by the news was BT's Eurosterling debt, dealers said.

Spreads on it's most liquid bond, a 500 million stg 7.125 percent September 2003 bond, widened the most. It had been trading at around 15 basis points through gilts in the past week but was at around six/one over gilts at 1000 GMT, traders said.
But other traders said any moves were merely a "knee-jerk reaction" to the weekend news and the real trades would only occur once the merger had gone through.
Added to this, the possibility of AT&T blocking the deal was holding off trades, they said.
The merger would create a $54 billion group called Concert Plc -- the world's second-largest telecommunications group based on market capitalisation behind Japan's NTT Corp.

The merger creates the first global communications company, with trans-global customers, a multinational management team, dual transatlantic headquarters and shares traded on three stock exchanges world wide.
"This is not a pebble we're throwing onto a quiet pool. It is a big rock, and its going to make a big splash," BT chairman Sir Iain Vallance told a news conference in New York on Sunday.
